transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I can’t stop checking my spreadsheets and calculations over and over. I’ll stay at work for hours after everyone else has left, even if I’ve already checked them. If I don’t do it just one more time, I feel like something bad will happen and it’ll be my fault.
Do these fears about making a mistake and something bad happening feel intrusive and unwanted to you?

Yes. I know the numbers match, but then I get this thought that I missed some hidden mistake—like in payroll or taxes—and someone’s check won’t go through, or the firm will get in trouble because of me. I try to push it away, but it just comes back. It feels like I can’t trust my own eyes.
When you go back to check the spreadsheets again, does it temporarily reduce the anxiety from the thought that you might have missed a mistake?
Yes, it does, but only for a little while. I check it again and feel calmer, like maybe I caught whatever I missed. Then the doubt comes back and I feel like I have to go over it one more time.
Do you also get repetitive unwanted thoughts like this at other times even when you are not checking anything?

Yes. Even when I’m not looking at a spreadsheet, the thought just pops in that I missed some hidden payroll or tax mistake. I’ll think somebody’s check won’t go through, or the firm will get in trouble because of me. I try to tell myself the numbers matched, but it comes right back—I just don’t trust that I saw everything.
Do you feel that the amount of checking you do is excessive?

Yes. I mean, I know I’ve already checked the same spreadsheets and calculations, but I keep going back over them. Sometimes I stay for hours after everyone else has left because I feel like I have to check one more time. If I don’t, I feel like something bad will happen and it’ll be my fault.
Do you think your fear that you missed a hidden mistake is probably not true, or are you convinced it is true?
I know the numbers match, so part of me knows it’s probably not true. But the thought keeps coming back that there’s one hidden mistake I didn’t see, and then I can’t trust my own eyes.
About how much time each day do these checking rituals take up?

Hours, usually. I’ll stay after work and keep rechecking the same spreadsheets and calculations over and over, even though I’ve already looked at them. It feels like I have to do it one more time or something bad will happen because of a mistake I missed.
Besides checking, do you have any other repetitive actions or mental rituals that you feel driven to do?

Mostly it’s the checking. I keep going back through the spreadsheets and calculations again and again, even after I know I’ve checked them. I’ll stay for hours doing it because I feel like I have to check one more time, or something bad could happen and it would be my fault.
Do these checking habits feel like part of your personality and the right way to do things, or do they feel unwanted and against how you want to be?

They feel unwanted. I don’t want to be at work for hours going over the same things after everyone’s left. I know I’ve checked, but I still feel like I have to do it again or something bad will happen and it’ll be my fault.
Do you try to resist these checking urges?

I try to, especially when I know I’ve already checked it. But then I start worrying I missed something, and I end up going back over the spreadsheets again anyway. It’s really hard to stop once that feeling starts.
